minutes.headline: Commission approved Lake Shirley's whole-lake fluridone treatment plan for 2025, with a condition that test results go to the office.
minutes.summary: The commission heard the Lake Shirley annual report and a proposal for a whole-lake herbicide treatment against fanwort, which now covers most survey sites. It approved the plan by roll call, adding a condition that testing results be sent to the office. It then heard the Hickory Hills annual report, which needed no action; spot-treatment requests are expected around May.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission approved the Lake Shirley 2025 whole-lake fluridone treatment plan by a 5-0 roll call vote.
The approval carries a condition that all testing results in the plan be sent to the office within a week of receipt.
The treatment targets fanwort, which was reported as now covering most survey sites on the lake.
The commission heard the Hickory Hills annual report and took no action; spot-treatment proposals are expected around May.
A member of the public asked whether removing plants with fluridone led to more algae the next year at Hickory Hills.

why_it_matters: A whole-lake herbicide treatment changes what happens in Lake Shirley this year, and the testing-results condition sets how the commission will see the effect on the water.
Hickory Hills spot-treatment requests are expected to return to the commission, so lake-weed control remains an open item for the neighborhoods around both lakes.
